For Federated Identity (Workload Identity): Not required, leave empty.

Workload Identity flag to identify if the backup location uses workload identity authentication.

  - Indicates that this backup location uses Workload Identity (OIDC) for authentication.
  - This flag is passed to the BackupLocation CR in Stork to inform it that workload identity is enabled.
  - Stork uses this flag to determine where to read credentials from:
    * If use_workload_identity=true: Stork reads cloud-specific configuration (e.g., azure_account_name, azure_subscription_id)
      from the backup location's config (e.g., S3Config) and uses workload identity for authentication.
    * If use_workload_identity=false: Stork reads credentials from the referenced cloud credential object secret (cloud_credential_ref).
  - When use_workload_identity=true, cloud_credential_ref should be empty or not set.
When set to false (default):
  - Indicates traditional authentication using cloud credentials stored in a CloudCredentialObject.
  - Stork reads authentication credentials from the cloud credential object referenced by cloud_credential_ref.

the namespace or virtual-machine name. They are not repeated here, both
because the embed would collide and because it makes a catalog row

ClaimOutcome.description:
Why a rule did or did not act on one resource.

ONE vocabulary, shared by every preview and every Drift Event -- journeys C4,
D5 and F11 each name an overlapping list, and three separate enums would drift
apart. A free-form string cannot be switched on by a client, cannot be counted,
and cannot be redacted per tier.

 - Applied: The rule acted.
 - WouldPlace: Preview only: what would happen if this rule ran now.
 - SkippedAlreadyPlaced: Skipped. Claiming only ever ADDS -- an existing assignment, Binding or
delegation is never overwritten.
 - SkippedClaimedByOtherRule: Lost arbitration to a stronger tier, or to an equally ranked older rule.
 - SkippedExcluded: Held out by an auto-rule exclusion.
 - FailedNoPlacement: Matched, but a Binding needs a placement first.
 - DepartedScopeAssignmentRetained: Stopped matching. The assignment and Binding are RETAINED.

can I restore for this namespace". This can NOT be derived by querying

is keyed by namespace NAME while identity here is the Kubernetes UID. A
namespace deleted and recreated under the same name is a different resource,
and a name-keyed lookup would hand it the earlier resource's history.

resource that failed inside a partially successful backup gets none, so its
timeline shows a gap and the SLA engine reports it out of SLA. That is how
per-resource failure isolation survives a shared execution.

Admin owns the inventory; an App Admin sees a namespace only once it has been
shared with them.

Write additionally lets them add a supplemental intent and edit hooks. Neither
lets them rebind, unbind, weaken the baseline, or see a destination: those are
refused by tier, not by the access level.

Sharing carries through the read path. A grantee who can see a resource can
see that resource's Bindings, recovery points and backups, because a share
that showed the resource but not its history would be useless.

azure_account_name.description:
Azure storage account name.
For Federated Identity (Workload Identity): Provide the account name here in the backup location.
  - When using federated identity authentication, the account name must be specified in the backup location
    because the AzureConfig credential object only contains client_id, tenant_id.
For Non-Federated Identity: Provide the account name in the AzureConfig credential object.
  - When using traditional authentication with client secret, the account name should be
    specified in the AzureConfig cloud credential object along with account_key or client_secret.

azure_subscription_id.description:
Azure subscription ID.
For Federated Identity (Workload Identity): Provide the subscription ID here in the backup location.
  - When using federated identity authentication, the subscription ID must be specified in the backup location.
For Non-Federated Identity: Provide the subscription ID in the AzureConfig credential object.
  - When using traditional authentication, the subscription ID should be specified in the
    AzureConfig cloud credential object.

google_project_id.description:
Google Cloud project ID.
For Federated Identity (Workload Identity): Required. Provide the project ID here in the backup location
  because no GoogleConfig cloud credential object is referenced.
For Non-Federated Identity: Not required. The project ID is automatically extracted from the
  JSON key in the GoogleConfig cloud credential object.

SLAPolicyAddIntentRequest.description:
One intent at a time, deliberately. A whole-object update could not tell
"one intent added" from "three rewritten", and the impact review needs the
exact change before it touches every Binding on this SLA Policy.

revision.description: Increases only. A recovery point records the revision it ran under.

paused.description: Suppresses new scheduled runs. Not a resource state.

paused_time.description: When it was suspended, and by whom. Needed to report the protection gap.

binding_count.description:
OUTPUT_ONLY, computed from an index on the Binding. A COUNT, not a list:
a list would be unbounded at fleet scale and every bind would have to
write this shared document.

SLAPolicyInfo.description:
A reusable, resource-agnostic set of Protection Intents. Holds no location,
no placement rule, no governance mode and no supplemental intent, so one SLA
Policy can serve resources in different clusters.

Metadata carries Ownership, so there is no owner field. There is no
back-reference list of Bindings either: it would be unbounded at fleet scale
and every bind would have to write this shared document. "Which Bindings use
this SLA Policy" is an index on the Binding.

frequency.description: Rendered for a human, for example "every 15 minutes".

derived_retain_count.description:
The derived copy count: ceil(period / longest gap), floored at 1.
A user states a business need and does not do this arithmetic --
7 days at 15 minutes is 672 copies per resource.

affected_resources.description:
Resources that lose coverage when this intent goes. Returned so the
caller can review the blast radius.
